title: Normalization formula for the arithmetic genus of a reduced proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $X$ a nonempty proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Give each irreducible component $X_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], let $\widetilde X_i	o X_i$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization], and let $
u:\widetilde X=\coprod_{i=1}^{v}\widetilde X_i	o X$ be their disjoint union. Then $v$ is finite, $
u$ is finite, each $\widetilde X_i$ is a smooth proper connected curve [def-sc-curves], and $F=
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}/\mathcal O_X$ is supported on finitely many closed points. Write $g_i=\dim_k H^1(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O_{\widetilde X_i})$ [def-sc-genus] and $\delta_X(y)=\dim_k F_y$ for a closed point $y$. With structure-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$p_a(X)=1-v+\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i+\sum_{y\in X	ext{ closed}}\delta_X(y).$$
Connectedness and nodality of $X$ are not assumed.

source.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.1 and its normalization exact sequence, printed p. 57; same Euler-characteristic identity for possibly disconnected curves. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Since $X$ is proper over $k$, it is of finite type. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] to the reduced finite-type scheme $X$: its irreducible components form a finite family and their componentwise normalization $\nu$ is finite and surjective. The same node supplies a dense open normal locus $N\subseteq X$ over which $\nu$ is an isomorphism.

Each $X_i$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its dimension is one by the pure-dimension hypothesis. It is proper over $k$ because it is a closed subscheme of the proper scheme $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore is of finite type. Apply [lem-sc-normalization-properties](a),(c): $\widetilde X_i$ is proper, has dimension one, and is smooth since $k$ is perfect. Here perfectness follows directly from algebraic closedness: in positive characteristic every $a\in k$ has a $p$-th root, and in characteristic zero all irreducible polynomials are separable. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] with the generic point of $X_i$ and the degree-one extension $k(X_i)/k(X_i)$; its normalization is exactly the integral-closure construction of [def-sc-normalization], and is integral, hence nonempty and connected. Thus every $\widetilde X_i$ is a smooth proper connected curve.

source.place: Tags 035L (lemma-normal-normalization), 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper); varieties.tex Tag 0BXR; normalization smoothness in dimension one as in lem-sc-normalization-properties(c).

proof.text: The map $\mathcal O_X\to\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$ is injective. Indeed, on an affine open $U\subseteq X$, if a section $s$ pulls back to zero, its restriction to each $U\cap X_i$ is zero: normalization of an integral scheme embeds its affine coordinate ring into its function field, by the integral-closure construction [def-sc-normalization]. Every point of $U$ lies on a component, so $s$ vanishes in every residue field. In the notation of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](1), this says $s\in\mathcal I_X(U)=\sqrt{(0)}$. This ideal is zero since $\mathcal O_X(U)$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Consequently $0\to\mathcal O_X\to B\to F\to0$, with $B=\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$, is exact by the definition of the quotient sheaf $F$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), injectivity in the normalization sequence; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01J1 (lemma-reduced).

proof.text: Since $X$ is locally Noetherian and $\nu$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] applied to $\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$ gives coherence of $B$. The cokernel clause of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] gives coherence of $F$ in step 3. Its support $S=\{y:F_y\ne0\}$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed].

On the dense normal open $N$ of step 1 the normalization is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], so $F|_N=0$. Every generic point of an irreducible component belongs to $N$. A closed subset of a one-dimensional Noetherian space avoiding all component generic points has dimension at most zero: a chain of two distinct irreducible closed subsets inside it would, after containment in a component, extend to a chain of length two in that component. Thus $\dim S\le0$. Apply [lem-sc-dim0-finite] to the closed subset $S$ of the finite-type $k$-scheme $X$: it is a finite set of closed points.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant); finiteness of zero-dimensional closed subsets as in lem-sc-dim0-finite.

proof.text: The germs map $\Gamma(X,F)\to\bigoplus_{y\in S}F_y$ is an isomorphism. It is injective because a section with zero germs at $S$ has zero germs everywhere. For surjectivity choose a representative $t$ of a germ at $y$ on an open neighbourhood $U_y$ avoiding $S\setminus\{y\}$. On $U_y\setminus\{y\}$ the sheaf is zero, so $t$ glues with zero on $X\setminus\{y\}$ to a global section with just that germ. Summing these sections over the finite set $S$ realizes any tuple. These operations are $k$-linear. This is the elementary sheaf-gluing argument for part (2) of Stacks Tag 0AYT, and also works when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), part (2); the germs and gluing argument is written out here.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] hold for $F$: it is coherent on the proper scheme $X$ and has zero-dimensional support. Hence its higher cohomology vanishes and $\chi(X,F)=\dim_k\Gamma(X,F)$. This space is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined]. The isomorphism in step 6 therefore also makes each $F_y$ finite-dimensional, and gives $\chi(X,F)=\sum_{y\in S}\dim_kF_y=\sum_{y\in X\text{ closed}}\delta_X(y)$; the last sum is finite since the other stalks are zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), parts (2)--(4); finiteness of coherent cohomology on a proper scheme.

proof.text: For each $i$, the proper finite-type curve $\widetilde X_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] in dimension one to obtain $H^q(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>1$. The smooth proper connected curve has $H^0(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O)=k$ by [lem-sc-global-functions]. Its first cohomology has dimension $g_i$ by [def-sc-genus]. Thus the Euler sum of [def-pc-euler-characteristic] gives $\chi(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O)=1-g_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BY7 (definition-genus); cohomology.tex Tag 02UZ (proposition-vanishing-Noetherian); varieties.tex Tag 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Let $h_i:\widetilde X_i\to X$ be the composite through the closed immersion $X_i\hookrightarrow X$. A closed immersion is finite directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: the inverse image of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, a cyclic $A$-module. Since $\widetilde X_i\to X_i$ is finite, stability under composition [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] makes $h_i$ finite. Its pushforward $G_i=h_{i,*}\mathcal O_{\widetilde X_i}$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent]. Sections of a sheaf on a disjoint union are the product of the sections on its summands by the sheaf gluing axiom. Hence the definition of direct image gives $B=\prod_iG_i=\bigoplus_iG_i$, since there are finitely many summands.

source.place: Tag 01WH (definition-integral), definition of finite morphism; finite composition; coherent.tex Tag 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent).

proof.text: For each finite $h_i$, which is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] identifies $H^q(X,G_i)$ with $H^q(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O)$ for every $q$, compatibly with the $k$-action from the structure maps. Taking the alternating dimensions yields $\chi(X,G_i)=1-g_i$ by step 8. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] successively to the split exact sequences of partial sums of the coherent modules $G_i$ (finite sums are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]). Step 9 then gives $\chi(X,B)=\sum_i(1-g_i)=v-\sum_i g_i$.

Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the coherent short exact sequence of step 3. It gives $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=\chi(X,B)-\chi(X,F)=v-\sum_i g_i-\sum_y\delta_X(y)$ by steps 7 and 10. Subtract this equality from $1$ and use the stated definition $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ to obtain the required formula. No step used connectedness or nodality of $X$.

source.place: Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive); Tag 0C1R normalization sequence and Tag 0AYT zero-dimensional contribution; arithmetic substitution.
